Method

How we calculate

Last updated 14 November 2026

The engine, the conventions and the checks behind every chart, panchang, timing and numerology result on VediCosmic, and the limits you should know about.

01Everything is calculated on your device

Every chart, panchang and timing on VediCosmic is worked out in your browser. Birth dates, times and places are not sent to us or anyone else; a place search downloads our list of places that start with the same letter, so only that first letter reaches our server. Planet positions come from Astronomy Engine 2.1.19, an open-source library (MIT licence) accurate to about one arcminute; the rest of the method is our own code, described below and checked against the reference values at the end of this page.

02Zodiac and ayanamsa

Positions are sidereal, using the Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsa in its mean form, without nutation: 23.2455° on 21 March 1956, carried to other dates by the IAU 1976 rate of precession. Planet positions are first referred to the mean equinox of date and the ayanamsa is then subtracted, the same convention Swiss Ephemeris uses. Signs are 30° each, nakshatras 13°20′ and padas 3°20′.

Tools that use this: Kundli (Vedic Birth Chart), Nakshatra Finder

03Lagna and houses

The Lagna (Ascendant) comes from local mean sidereal time, the mean obliquity of the ecliptic and your latitude, then has the ayanamsa subtracted. Houses are whole signs: the Lagna’s sign is the first house, the next sign the second, and so on.

The Lagna moves about one degree every four minutes, so it depends on an accurate birth time. The chart tells you when the Lagna changes sign within five minutes of the time you entered. Beyond 66° latitude, where some signs never rise, no Lagna is given.

Tools that use this: Kundli (Vedic Birth Chart)

04Grahas

Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus and Saturn are apparent geocentric positions. Rahu is the mean lunar node and Ketu the point opposite it; as mean nodes they always move backwards. A planet is marked retrograde when its longitude is decreasing over the day around the birth time.

Tools that use this: Kundli (Vedic Birth Chart)

05Time and place

A birth time is read in the time zone of the birth place, using the time-zone database built into your browser. That covers daylight saving and historic changes, such as India’s +6:30 war time (1942–45) or Nepal’s move from +5:30 to +5:45 in 1986. If the clocks went back and the time happened twice, the chart says so and lets you choose; if the clocks went forward and the time never existed, it says that too.

Until the 1950s some Indian cities kept their own local time (Bombay and Calcutta time, for example). The database does not always know these, so the place search has an “Advanced” option to enter the offset written on an old record.

Places come from GeoNames (CC BY 4.0): every town of 1,000 people or more in India and Nepal, and cities of 15,000 or more elsewhere. If your town is missing, enter its coordinates under “Advanced”.

Tools that use this: Kundli (Vedic Birth Chart), Nakshatra Finder, Rahu Kaal & Muhurat Finder, Hora Calculator, Ekadashi & Vrat Calendar

06Panchang and daily timings

The panchang day runs from sunrise to the next sunrise. Sunrise and sunset are the moments the Sun’s upper edge meets a sea-level horizon, with standard atmospheric refraction (34′).

  • Tithi: the Moon’s lead over the Sun in steps of 12°; karana: half a tithi.
  • Nakshatra: the Moon’s sidereal position; yoga: the sum of the Sun’s and Moon’s sidereal positions, in steps of 13°20′.
  • The value in force at sunrise is shown with the time it ends, found to within a second and shown to the nearest minute.
  • Rahu Kaal, Yamaganda and Gulika Kaal: one of eight equal parts of the daytime, chosen by weekday.
  • Abhijit muhurta: the eighth of fifteen equal parts of the daytime (traditionally not used on Wednesdays). Brahma muhurta: 96 to 48 minutes before sunrise.
  • Choghadiya: eight equal parts of the day and eight of the night, in the traditional order for each weekday. Horas: twelve equal parts of each.

Tools that use this: Rahu Kaal & Muhurat Finder, Hora Calculator, Daily Sādhana

07Vrat dates

Ekadashi, Purnima, Amavasya and Durga Ashtami fall on the day whose sunrise is in that tithi; Pradosh on the day the Trayodashi tithi is in force during the 2 h 24 min after sunset; Sankashti Chaturthi on the day the Krishna Chaturthi tithi is in force at moonrise. A tithi that starts and ends between two sunrises belongs to the day it falls in. Some traditions use other rules (the Vaishnava rule for Ekadashi, for example), which can move a date by a day.

Tools that use this: Ekadashi & Vrat Calendar, Daily Sādhana

08Vimshottari dasha

The first period belongs to the lord of the Moon’s birth nakshatra, and the share of it still to run is the share of the nakshatra the Moon had yet to cross. Periods follow the order Ketu 7 years, Venus 20, Sun 6, Moon 10, Mars 7, Rahu 18, Jupiter 16, Saturn 19, Mercury 17, with years of 365.25 days; sub-periods are in the same proportions.

Tools that use this: Kundli (Vedic Birth Chart)

09Numerology: one method on every page

The numerology calculators share one set of rules (VediCosmic numerology 1.0.0), so a date of birth gives the same Mulank, Bhagyank and Life Path on whichever page you enter it. Dates are handled as plain day, month and year numbers, so the result never shifts with your time zone, and an impossible date such as 31 February is refused.

Numerology has no independent reference to test against in the way astronomy has. Our tests fix this method and keep every page on it; they cannot show that the method is the right one. Where teachers differ, the sections below say which rule we follow.

Tools that use this: Lo Shu Grid Calculator, Life Path Number Calculator, Numerology Calculator, Chaldean Numerology Calculator, Mobile Number Numerology

10Lo Shu grid, Driver, Conductor and Kua

  • Driver (Mulank): the day of the month added down to one digit. Conductor (Bhagyank): every digit of the full date added down to one digit. Neither keeps 11, 22 or 33.
  • Grid: every digit of the day, month and four-digit year is written in its cell of the square, whose rows are 4 9 2, 3 5 7 and 8 1 6. Zero has no cell and is left out.
  • Added numbers: the Conductor and the Kua number are written into the grid as well. So is the Driver, except when the birth day is 1 to 9, 10, 20 or 30, because that day already puts the Driver’s digit in the grid.
  • Kua: the digits of the calendar year of birth added down to one digit; 11 minus that digit for a man, 4 plus that digit for a woman, added down again. A result of 5 is read as 2 for a man and 8 for a woman.
  • Lines: the three rows, three columns and two diagonals are each reported as complete, two of three, one of three or empty.
  • Kua directions: the four favourable directions of the Eight Mansions school of feng shui for each Kua number.

Other teachers fill the grid from the date digits alone, write the Driver every time, use only the last two digits of the year, or leave the Kua out. Feng shui teachers who count the Chinese solar year use the previous year for births before 4 February; the Lo Shu page tells you when that would change your Kua. Each of these is one setting in our code, so a rule can be changed and re-tested in one place.

Tools that use this: Lo Shu Grid Calculator, Numerology Calculator, Life Path Number Calculator

11Life Path and the Western name numbers

  • Life Path: the month, the day and the year are each added down first, keeping 11, 22 and 33, then added together and reduced again. Adding all eight digits in one line always gives the same single digit but can give a different master number; where it does, the page shows both.
  • Name numbers use the Pythagorean letter values (A, J, S = 1 through I, R = 9), word by word. Expression takes every letter, Soul Urge the vowels A, E, I, O and U, and Personality the consonants. Y is always a consonant.
  • Personal year: the birth month and day added to the calendar year, reduced to one digit; it changes on 1 January. Personal month adds the calendar month, and personal day the day of the month.
  • Pinnacles: month plus day, day plus year, the sum of those two, and month plus year, each from single digits. The first ends at 36 minus the Life Path digit and the next two last nine years each. Challenges are the differences between the same pairs.

Tools that use this: Life Path Number Calculator, Numerology Calculator

12Chaldean name numbers

Letter values are those printed by Cheiro (Count Louis Hamon) in his Book of Numbers, 1926: A, I, J, Q, Y = 1; B, K, R = 2; C, G, L, S = 3; D, M, T = 4; E, H, N, X = 5; U, V, W = 6; O, Z = 7; F, P = 8. No letter is 9, and a digit typed in a name keeps its own value.

The compound number is the total of the whole name and the root is that total added down to one digit. Cheiro describes the compounds from 10 to 52; a larger total has its digits added until it falls in that range. His readings are restated in plain words, and his sterner warnings are given as cautions about conduct, not as forecasts.

Tools that use this: Chaldean Numerology Calculator, Numerology Calculator

13Friendly numbers

Indian numerology gives each number a planet: 1 Sun, 2 Moon, 3 Jupiter, 4 Rahu, 5 Mercury, 6 Venus, 7 Ketu, 8 Saturn, 9 Mars. Wherever a page speaks of friendly numbers, lucky numbers, the harmony of Driver and Conductor, or how a mobile number sits with a date of birth, it reads one table of friendships between those planets.

For the seven visible planets the table is the natural friendship (naisargika maitri) of the Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra. Rahu and Ketu are not in that list, so we follow the convention most teachers use: Rahu sides with Mercury, Venus and Saturn, and Ketu with Mars, Venus and Saturn. No page turns these friendships into a percentage or a single verdict, because the tradition offers no arithmetic for one.

Tools that use this: Mobile Number Numerology, Lo Shu Grid Calculator, Life Path Number Calculator

14How we check the results

Every change to the site runs automated tests against reference values made with independent software that is not part of the site. The tolerances are fixed in advance and are never loosened to make a test pass.

Reference checks, tolerances and the largest differences found
CheckToleranceLargest difference
Ayanamsa, 8 dates 1900–2100 (Swiss Ephemeris)0.002°0.0001°
Lagna, 18 charts (Swiss Ephemeris)sign exact, 0.02°0.002° (7″)
Nine grahas, 3 charts (Swiss Ephemeris)0.02°0.0015° (5″)
Sunrise and sunset, 240 days (NASA JPL DE421)1 minute3 seconds
Tithi, nakshatra, yoga and karana end times, 240 days (NASA JPL DE421)2 minutes12 seconds

The panchang days are 20 places — from Thiruvananthapuram to Srinagar, plus Kathmandu, Dubai, Singapore, London, New York, Toronto and Sydney — on 12 dates of 2026, including daylight-saving changes. The reference charts we pass are listed below. One of them (L01) has the Moon 0.009° from the end of the zodiac; the chart marks it as borderline, because no calculation can promise which side such a Moon falls.

The numerology rules are checked differently, since there is nothing independent to compare them with: 26 cases worked out by hand must match exactly, every date from 1900 to 2099 is tested for a consistent grid, and the Conductor must equal the Life Path digit on all of them.

16Known limits

  • A birth time that is a few minutes out can change the Lagna, and an hour can change the Moon’s nakshatra. The charts say when this is likely.
  • Old local times: before the 1950s the time written on a record may not be the time the zone database assumes. Use the “Advanced” offset if you know it.
  • Sunrise is for a sea-level horizon; hills, buildings and altitude can shift what you see by a few minutes.
  • The reference checks cover 1900–2100. Dates far outside that range have not been checked.
  • Regional panchangs can differ on vrat rules, so a date may differ by a day from your family’s calendar.
  • Astrology and numerology are traditions of reflection, not sciences of prediction. See the disclaimer.
